title: Riveted Plate
summary: Tier-1 Warrior Bulwark passive (max rank 5) that steadily increases flat armor for frontline durability.

p: Reinforces armor seams, adding flat physical defense.

Thornwick sergeants inspect every recruit's rivets before dawn, knowing a loose strap kills faster than a gnoll spear. Doubling the iron over the ribs adds weight on the march, yet nobody complains once arrows start falling.

title: Oak Rim Guard
summary: Tier-1 Warrior Bulwark passive (max rank 5) that raises shield block chance against incoming attacks.

p: Improves shield block angle against frontal strikes.

Green soldiers flinch behind their shields and take the blow on the flat; veterans angle the oak rim to glance steel aside. A well-placed iron boss turns a fatal cleaver swing into nothing more than a bruised forearm.

title: Shield Bash
summary: Tier-2 Warrior Bulwark active skill (max rank 3) requiring Oak Rim Guard, stunning an enemy with a heavy shield slam.

p: Active: Slams shield into foe, stunning 1.5s and interrupting.

Nothing ends a shaman's sermon faster than forty pounds of tarred oak driven straight into his teeth. Levy instructors drill this move until recruits can land it ankle-deep in river mud without losing their footing.

title: Brace the Ditch
summary: Tier-2 Warrior Bulwark passive (max rank 4) requiring Riveted Plate, boosting resistance against ranged missiles.

p: Reduces knockback and incoming ranged damage while stationary.

Holding a wet ditch under quill-fiend fire teaches a man to tuck his chin and angle his shoulders by instinct. What looks like cowering from afar is actually the reason half the Vanguard Company still has both eyes.

title: Gorget of Iron
summary: Tier-3 Warrior Bulwark passive (max rank 4) requiring Brace the Ditch, granting a substantial boost to maximum health.

p: Increases maximum health and resistance to bleed effects.

A high iron collar chafes the jaw and collects rainwater, yet veterans refuse to march without one. When a sand-raider's scimitar slides off your pauldron, that ugly strip of plate earns its weight in crowns.

title: Lock Shields
summary: Tier-3 Warrior Bulwark active skill (max rank 3) requiring Shield Bash, granting bonus armor to the entire party.

p: Active: Grants nearby allies +6 armor for 6s.

One shield is a door; six shields overlapped at the knee are a stone wall. When the sergeant barks the order, even nervous militia remember to lean into their neighbor's rim and let the charge break itself.

title: Stubborn Marrow
summary: Tier-4 Warrior Bulwark passive (max rank 2) requiring Gorget of Iron, giving a chance to survive fatal blows.

p: Survives a lethal blow once per battle at 15% HP.
Some borderers are simply too stubborn to die before their pay-chit clears. Even after a blow that should drop an ox, sheer grit and thick northern bone keep them upright long enough to swing back.

title: Living Bastion
summary: Tier-4 Warrior Bulwark capstone (max rank 2) requiring Lock Shields, sharply reducing incoming damage during heavy assaults.

p: Active: Roots self for 6s, cutting all damage taken by 50%.

At the Alder Bridge stand, three pikemen held a collapsed arch for half an hour while refugees crossed behind them. Living Bastion is that same refusal to yield, honed into a discipline that laughs at siege engines.

title: Heavy Edge
summary: Tier-1 Warrior Reaver passive (max rank 5) that increases base melee damage across all close-quarters strikes.

p: Increases melee physical weapon damage.
Border smiths leave a little extra iron behind the sweet spot of a blade because fancy balance does not split a flintback's shell. Put your hips into the swing and let gravity finish the argument.

title: Quarry Swing
summary: Tier-1 Warrior Reaver passive (max rank 5) that adds armor penetration to break through plated foes.

p: Adds bonus armor penetration against plated foes.
Learned from escaped Deep Quarry miners who knew exactly where a basalt seam cracks under a pickaxe. Apply the same angle to an imperial breastplate and the rivets pop like dry peas.

title: Cleaving Arc
summary: Tier-2 Warrior Reaver active skill (max rank 4) requiring Heavy Edge, sweeping melee damage across multiple nearby foes.

p: Active: Sweeps weapon in a frontal arc hitting up to 3 foes.
When briar-hounds or gnolls crowd your flanks, careful fencing gets you chewed to pieces. A wide, brutal arc clears breathing room in a single heartbeat and reminds the pack to keep its distance.

title: Bloodied Grip
summary: Tier-2 Warrior Reaver passive (max rank 4) requiring Quarry Swing, restoring health whenever you fell an enemy.

p: Restores health on every melee kill.

Veterans never wipe their leather grips mid-fight; the tackiness keeps the hilt from twisting in wet hands. Dropping a foe brings a cold rush of relief that steadies the pulse and dulls fresh bruises.

title: Sunder Hinges
summary: Tier-3 Warrior Reaver active skill (max rank 3) requiring Cleaving Arc, stripping enemy armor to expose them to follow-up blows.

p: Melee critical hits reduce target armor by 4 for 6s.

Heavy knights rely on buckles, straps, and shoulder pins to stay intact. Aim for the iron hinges instead of the thick chest-plate, and even a dread knight turns soft enough for a levy spear to finish.

title: Breaker's Rush
summary: Tier-3 Warrior Reaver active skill (max rank 3) requiring Bloodied Grip, charging into enemies for heavy impact damage.

p: Active: Charges 4 tiles into enemy ranks, knocking back.

Developed by Ironcamp breachers who had to cross open ground before cliffside arbalests could wind their prods. Drop your shoulder, tuck your chin, and hit the enemy line like an unhitched supply wagon.

title: Grim Momentum
summary: Tier-4 Warrior Reaver passive (max rank 3) requiring Sunder Hinges, increasing attack speed as combat intensifies.

p: Each consecutive hit increases attack speed by 5% up to 25%.

Once a seasoned reaver finds his rhythm, the weight of the steel stops mattering. Each follow-through feeds directly into the next backswing, turning a slow two-handed maul into a relentless threshing flail.

title: Execution Sweep
summary: Tier-4 Warrior Reaver capstone (max rank 2) requiring Breaker's Rush, multiplying damage to finish weakened targets.

p: Active: Deals double melee damage to targets below 35% HP.

No mercy, no flourishes, and no wasted motion—just a single merciless cut meant to settle the account permanently. Quartermasters call it tidy work; survivors on the other side rarely call it anything at all.

title: Muster Discipline
summary: Tier-1 Warrior Banner passive (max rank 5) that strengthens morale resistance against fear and battlefield panic.

p: Increases squad maximum morale and fear resistance.

Fresh levies break at the first howl from the fog unless an officer stands where they can see his boots planted. Calm orders spoken at normal volume do more to hold a line than a dozen shouted threats.

title: Rationed Pace
summary: Tier-1 Warrior Banner passive (max rank 5) that reduces fatigue buildup during prolonged marches and battles.

p: Reduces party combat fatigue accumulation.

Running uphill in chainmail is a fine way to collapse before the fighting starts. Old Vanguard sergeants teach their men to breathe through the nose, shorten their stride, and save their wind for the breach.

title: Hold the Line
summary: Tier-2 Warrior Banner active skill (max rank 3) requiring Muster Discipline, sharply boosting block chance while holding ground.

p: Active: Commands squad to hold ground, gaining +15% block.
Plant the boot, lock the elbow, and refuse to give up one inch of mud. Even poorly equipped militia can stop a cavalry rush when they trust the man beside them not to turn tail.

title: Veteran's Eye
summary: Tier-2 Warrior Banner passive (max rank 4) requiring Rationed Pace, improving the accuracy of hired mercenaries.

p: Increases mercenary accuracy and critical chance.
Hired blades fight better when their commander actually calls targets instead of waving vaguely at the treeline. A sharp nod and a pointed gauntlet turn sloppy brawlers into disciplined flankers.

title: Hardened Pay
summary: Tier-3 Warrior Banner passive (max rank 4) requiring Veteran's Eye, lowering the gold upkeep required for mercenary squads.

p: Lowers mercenary upkeep wages per mission.

Mercenaries charge double when they think their captain is an idiot who will get them killed in a ditch. Prove you know how to read terrain and keep them fed, and they suddenly ask far less silver at payday.

title: Rallying Horn
summary: Tier-3 Warrior Banner active skill (max rank 3) requiring Hold the Line, restoring stamina to rally exhausted allies.

p: Active: Cleanses fear and restores 25 stamina to allies.

A battered brass horn blown over the din of clashing steel cuts straight through exhaustion. Men who thought their arms were lead find strength for one more push when the company call echoes across the field.

title: Iron Vanguard
summary: Tier-4 Warrior Banner passive (max rank 3) requiring Hardened Pay, projecting a damage aura that empowers nearby allies.

p: Allies within 4 tiles gain +12% physical damage.

When the Vanguard standard pushes forward through ash and arrow-fire, the whole line leans in behind it. Soldiers strike harder simply because they refuse to look cowardly next to a commander who never flinches.

title: Unbroken Standard
summary: Tier-4 Warrior Banner capstone (max rank 2) requiring Rallying Horn, granting a powerful haste surge to the company.

p: Active: Company refuses to rout and gains +25% speed for 8s.

Torn by buckshot, scorched by caldera embers, and patched with saddle-leather, the company banner still flies. Seeing it planted in the breach drives every man in earshot into a relentless, double-time assault.

title: Measured Draw
summary: Tier-1 Archer Deadeye passive (max rank 5) that increases base ranged damage with bows and crossbows.

p: Increases bow and arbalest piercing damage.

Hasty archers loose three shafts into the mud for every one that bites. Drawing cleanly to the jawbone and holding half a breath puts enough punch behind an ash arrow to punch straight through boiled hide.

title: Wind Reader
summary: Tier-1 Archer Deadeye passive (max rank 5) that improves ranged accuracy across open and stormy terrain.

p: Improves ranged accuracy and reduces distance penalty.

Between river fog in Thornwick and alkali gales in Redmarsh, an arrow rarely flies straight on its own. Good marksmen watch the grass tips and chimney smoke, aiming two hand-breadths upwind before they ever loose.

title: Aimed Throat-Shot
summary: Tier-2 Archer Deadeye active skill (max rank 4) requiring Measured Draw, dealing heavy critical damage to vulnerable spots.

p: Active: High-precision shot with +35% critical damage.
Even the heaviest dread knight has a thin seam between gorget and visor where leather shows through. Take your time, wait for him to raise his visor to shout, and end the battle with a single shaft.

title: High Ground
summary: Tier-2 Archer Deadeye passive (max rank 4) requiring Wind Reader, increasing ranged damage when firing from elevated ground.

p: Grants bonus range and damage when firing from elevation.

Canyon raiders in Twin Passes proved how ugly a fight gets when bowmen hold the ridge. Firing downhill adds gravity to the draw weight and lets a sharp eye pick off casters hiding behind tower shields.

title: Bodkin Penetration
summary: Tier-3 Archer Deadeye passive (max rank 4) requiring Aimed Throat-Shot, adding armor penetration to ranged attacks.

p: Ranged attacks ignore flat enemy armor.

Broadheads are for deer; narrow, four-sided bodkin points are for imperial plate. Driven by a heavy warbow, a well-tempered bodkin wedges right between iron links and splits them apart with a dry snap.

title: Double Nock
summary: Tier-3 Archer Deadeye active skill (max rank 2) requiring High Ground, loosing multiple arrows in a rapid sequence.

p: Active: Fires two arrows in rapid succession at one target.

Alder Ford toll-bowmen practiced holding a spare shaft between their bow-fingers to discourage bandits from rushing the gate. It ruins a proper stance, yet two arrows in the chest settle most arguments quickly.

title: Lethal Cadence
summary: Tier-4 Archer Deadeye passive (max rank 3) requiring Bodkin Penetration, reducing skill cooldowns on critical hits.

p: Critical hits refund 4 mana and shave 2s off cooldowns.
When every shot lands where you meant it, the whole battlefield slows down to a tidy rhythm. Draw, loose, watch the target fold, and nock again before the first feathered shaft stops quivering.

title: One Arrow, One Toll
summary: Tier-4 Archer Deadeye capstone (max rank 2) requiring Double Nock, firing a devastating piercing shot through a line of foes.

p: Active: Pierces a straight line of foes for 160% weapon dmg.

An old border grimace about thrift: why waste three good arrows on a column of raiders when one heavy shaft will do? Drawn past the ear on a reinforced stave, it punches clean through shield, rib, and the man behind.

title: Light Footing
summary: Tier-1 Archer Stalker passive (max rank 5) that increases movement speed for repositioning and kiting.

p: Increases movement speed and terrain traversal.

Heavy boots sink into bog-peat and announce your approach from fifty paces. Greywood poachers wrap their soles in greased rawhide, skimming over wet roots and loose scree without leaving a clear print.

title: Peat Camouflage
summary: Tier-1 Archer Stalker passive (max rank 5) that raises evasion chance against incoming attacks.

p: Boosts evasion against ranged attacks and ambushes.
Rubbing bog-mud and crushed alder leaves into a cloak ruins the wool, yet it makes a scout vanish ten paces off the trail. Even in open combat, a low, shifting stance throws off enemy aim.

title: Backstep Vault
summary: Tier-2 Archer Stalker active skill (max rank 3) requiring Light Footing, vaulting backward to escape melee threats.

p: Active: Leaps 3 tiles backward, leaving a slowing caltrop.

When a thorn-boar or sand-raider closes inside spear-length, standing your ground is just prideful suicide. Kick off the nearest rock, clear three paces in a single bound, and loose while they are still turning.

title: Fen Sightlines
summary: Tier-2 Archer Stalker passive (max rank 4) requiring Peat Camouflage, expanding vision range across fog and darkness.

p: Expands fog-of-war vision radius and trap detection.

Most travelers stare straight at the boardwalk and walk right into an ambush. Fen-stalkers scan the waterline for disturbed reeds and unnatural ripples, spotting threats long before the lantern-light reaches them.

title: Flanking Instinct
summary: Tier-3 Archer Stalker passive (max rank 3) requiring Backstep Vault, boosting damage when striking enemies from the flank.

p: Attacks from behind or side deal +25% bonus damage.
Hitting a shielded man from the front is work for a warrior with a heavy mace. Slip around his blind side while he trades blows with your vanguard, and every rib is wide open.

title: Hamstring Trap
summary: Tier-3 Archer Stalker active skill (max rank 3) requiring Fen Sightlines, deploying a trap that roots pursuing enemies.

p: Active: Places a concealed snare that roots foes for 3.5s.

Adapted from iron wolf-gins used along the northern timberlines, scaled up with notched jaws to catch charging beasts and raiders. Nothing ruins a berserker's momentum like stepping into hidden teeth in the grass.

title: Ghost in the Reeds
summary: Tier-4 Archer Stalker passive (max rank 3) requiring Flanking Instinct, granting temporary stealth to break enemy focus.

p: Entering smoke or brush grants 2s of untargetable stealth.

Drop low into the sedge, let the smoke drift across your shoulders, and stay motionless for two heartbeats. By the time the enemy archers figure out where you went, you are already behind their casters.

title: Ambush Volley
summary: Tier-4 Archer Stalker capstone (max rank 2) requiring Hamstring Trap, unleashing a multi-arrow ambush volley.

p: Active: Fires 5 rapid poisoned shafts while retreating.

The signature trick of Greywood's most wanted poachers when cornered by bailiff patrols. Step out of cover with five shafts fanned between your fingers and turn a quiet clearing into a wall of fletching.

title: Goose-Wing Fletch
summary: Tier-1 Archer Fletcher passive (max rank 5) that increases ranged attack speed for faster volleys.

p: Increases arrow flight speed and attack rate.
Crooked feathers wobble in crosswinds and slow down the draw. Trimming stiff grey goose-pinions by hand lets an archer nock and loose cleanly without ever glancing down at the quiver.

title: Waxed Bowstring
summary: Tier-1 Archer Fletcher passive (max rank 5) that reduces mana costs for archer skills and special shots.

p: Reduces mana cost of archer active skills.
Wet hemp stretches and snaps in the Thornwick drizzle, ruining a bowman's rhythm. Rubbing beeswax and pine resin into the cord keeps the draw crisp and conserves strength through long skirmishes.

title: Pitch-Tipped Shaft
summary: Tier-2 Archer Fletcher active skill (max rank 4) requiring Goose-Wing Fletch, firing burning arrows that deal fire damage over time.

p: Active: Fires an incendiary arrow that ignites ground.
Wrap tow-rag behind the iron head, dip it in wagon-pitch, and touch it to a trench brazier. It ruins the arrow's range slightly, yet nothing clears out a crypt embalmer or spore-matron faster.

title: Salvage Quiver
summary: Tier-2 Archer Fletcher passive (max rank 4) requiring Waxed Bowstring, restoring mana when looting or recovering arrows.

p: Recovers mana and health when looting fallen enemies.

Good shafts are too expensive on the Border to leave sticking out of dead gnolls. Pulling unbroken arrows back out of the mud keeps a practical hunter supplied long after the baggage train falls behind.

title: Bile-Dipped Broads
summary: Tier-3 Archer Fletcher passive (max rank 4) requiring Pitch-Tipped Shaft, amplifying poison damage dealt by ranged attacks.

p: Increases poison damage and duration dealt by the archer.
Redmarsh vipers and fen-toads yield a thick green bile that clings well to notched broadheads. Even a shallow scratch across a raider's wrist turns nasty before he can cross the clearing.

title: Shatter-Flint Head
summary: Tier-3 Archer Fletcher active skill (max rank 3) requiring Salvage Quiver, firing flint-tipped arrows that burst into shrapnel.

p: Active: Blasts target with quartz shrapnel in 2-tile radius.

When iron runs short, border fletchers knap brittle grey chert into jagged heads that shatter on impact against shields. The target takes the shaft; everyone standing elbow-to-elbow beside him takes the splinters.

title: Master Bowyer
summary: Tier-4 Archer Fletcher passive (max rank 3) requiring Bile-Dipped Broads, granting broad bow mastery and improved performance.

p: Adds +15% weapon damage to all equipped bows and crossbows.

Years of seasoning yew staves, scraping horn bellies, and balancing draw weights teach a hunter every quirk of his weapon. In a master bowyer's hands, even a salvaged frontier bow shoots like a guild prize.

title: Storm of Bodkins
summary: Tier-4 Archer Fletcher capstone (max rank 2) requiring Shatter-Flint Head, raining multiple waves of arrows over an area.

p: Active: Calls a 3-wave arrow barrage over a wide zone.

Borrowed from Oakhaven's seawall drills, where a single veteran archer had to pin down an entire boarding boat alone. Loose high into the wind in rapid waves until the flagstones look like a harrowed field.

title: Thermal Gradient
summary: Tier-1 Mage Pyromancy passive (max rank 5) that increases all fire spell damage.

p: Increases fire spell damage.
Collegium apprentices spend their first winter learning that fire is not magic—it is just impatient heat. Push the gradient sharp enough and damp wool catches flame even in a northern downpour.

title: Singed Cuffs
summary: Tier-1 Mage Pyromancy passive (max rank 5) that grants fire resistance to weather heat and enemy flames.

p: Grants fire resistance and reduces self-burn hazard damage.

Every practicing pyromancer eventually burns off his eyebrows and ruins two good sleeves. The ones who survive learn to weave a thin thermal cushion around their wrists before calling anything hotter than a candle.

title: Cinder Lance
summary: Tier-2 Mage Pyromancy active skill (max rank 4) requiring Thermal Gradient, hurling a piercing lance of condensed flame.

p: Active: Fires a piercing bolt of white-hot slag.
Wide fireballs waste mana on empty mud and risk scorching your own pikemen. Condensing the blaze into a narrow white-hot spear punches cleanly through armored ranks without singeing the vanguard.

title: Dry Tinder
summary: Tier-2 Mage Pyromancy passive (max rank 3) requiring Singed Cuffs, amplifying burning damage over time on ignited foes.

p: Ignited enemies take +15% increased damage from all sources.
Oil-soaked leather, dry linen wrappings, and pitch-tarred shields all burn wonderfully once you know how to feed the draft. A skilled pyromancer lets the enemy's own gear finish the work for him.

title: Exothermic Surge
summary: Tier-3 Mage Pyromancy passive (max rank 3) requiring Cinder Lance, restoring mana whenever a burning enemy dies.

p: Killing a burning foe restores 12 mana.
Collegium thermodynamicists insist no heat is ever truly lost—it merely changes hands. Reclaiming the dying flare from a fallen target lets a caster keep firing long after his mana flasks run dry.

title: Slag Conduit
summary: Tier-3 Mage Pyromancy active skill (max rank 3) requiring Dry Tinder, raising a lasting wall of fire to block and scorch foes.

p: Active: Creates a wall of fire across 4 tiles for 5s.

Inspired by Ironcamp's slag-channels, which turn narrow alleys into impassable trenches of glowing rock. Drop a burning barrier across a bridge arch and watch charging beasts think twice about crossing.

title: Controlled Meltdown
summary: Tier-4 Mage Pyromancy passive (max rank 3) requiring Exothermic Surge, expanding the area of effect of fire spells.

p: Fire AoE spells gain +25% radius and critical chance.

The Collegium forbids widening a combustion radius past three paces inside city walls for obvious reasons. Out in the ash-wastes, however, letting the blast bloom wide clears entire packs in one cast.

title: Caldera Eruption
summary: Tier-4 Mage Pyromancy capstone (max rank 2) requiring Slag Conduit, triggering a massive volcanic eruption for heavy fire damage.

p: Active: Detonates molten rock under target for heavy AoE.

Channeling the raw pressure pulsing beneath the Obsidian Caldera is reckless work that leaves boots smoking. When the ground splits and white-hot cinders geyser skyward, nothing left standing remembers why it charged.

title: Copper Grounding
summary: Tier-1 Mage Tempest passive (max rank 5) that increases storm and lightning spell damage.

p: Increases lightning and cold spell damage.

Fools try to throw lightning with bare heels in a puddle and end up smoking beside their own staff. A length of copper wire stitched down the boot-sole lets a caster push twice the voltage without cooking himself.

title: Static Lattice
summary: Tier-1 Mage Tempest passive (max rank 5) that accelerates spell casting speed.

p: Boosts lightning resistance and cast speed.

By holding a light charge across the knuckles, a tempest mage keeps his fingers snapping through gestures faster than the eye can follow. The only drawback is that metal door-latches bite back for hours afterward.

title: Galvanic Arc
summary: Tier-2 Mage Tempest active skill (max rank 3) requiring Copper Grounding, unleashing lightning that jumps between multiple foes.

p: Active: Zaps target and jumps to 2 nearby foes.

Armored soldiers standing shoulder-to-shoulder make a lovely circuit. One sharp snap from the fingertips leaps from breastplate to helm down the line, leaving the whole formation twitching in the rain.

title: Rime Coat
summary: Tier-2 Mage Tempest passive (max rank 4) requiring Static Lattice, extending chill duration on enemies.

p: Cold spells chill enemies 15% longer.

Northern casters learned to lace their frost spells with river-mist so the rime clings to wool and leather long after the bolt fades. A chilled raider swings like he is wading through waist-deep mire, giving the vanguard plenty of time to finish him.

title: Wet Conduction
summary: Tier-3 Mage Tempest passive (max rank 3) requiring Galvanic Arc, amplifying storm damage against wet targets.

p: Lightning spells deal +30% damage to chilled or wet foes.

Thornwick's endless drizzle is a misery for bowmen and a gift for tempest arcanists. Soaked mail conducts lightning straight to the ribs, turning a routine river-ford skirmish into a brisk lesson in Collegium physics.

title: Hoarfrost Ring
summary: Tier-3 Mage Tempest active skill (max rank 3) requiring Rime Coat, unleashing a freezing nova around the caster.

p: Active: Freezes adjacent melee attackers solid for 2.5s.

When briar-hounds break past the pike line, a smart mage does not try to outrun them in wet robes. Slamming a ring of flash-frost into the mud locks the whole pack in brittle ice long enough to step back and reload.

title: Ley-Line Capacitor
summary: Tier-4 Mage Tempest passive (max rank 4) requiring Wet Conduction, significantly expanding the caster's maximum mana.

p: Increases maximum mana and out-of-combat mana regen.

Inspired by the copper-bound leyden horns mounted on Redmarsh wardstones, this technique stores surplus ambient charge inside the caster's own focus. The air around them smells permanently of storm-ozone and wet iron.

title: Ball Lightning
summary: Tier-4 Mage Tempest capstone (max rank 2) requiring Hoarfrost Ring, conjuring a slow-moving orb that zaps nearby foes.

p: Active: Launches a slow orb that shocks every 0.5s.

Unstable, humming, and deeply unpopular with friendly pike-sergeants, a drifting sphere of bottled lightning chews through packed formations at its own leisurely pace. Even seasoned dread knights break ranks rather than stand beside it.

title: Chalk Geometry
summary: Tier-1 Mage Wardcraft passive (max rank 5) that increases maximum mana for sustained spellcasting.

p: Increases maximum mana pool.

First-year Collegium students spend months drawing clean circles on slate floors with cheap border chalk. Sloppy angles leak mana into the floorboards; crisp geometry keeps enough reserve in the tank for a second volley.

title: Vellum Margin
summary: Tier-1 Mage Wardcraft passive (max rank 5) that steadily boosts mana regeneration during combat.

p: Improves mana regeneration per second.

Experienced scribes never crowd their ink to the edge of the page, leaving wide margins for corrections and breath. Applying the same discipline to spellcraft lets an arcanist recover focus between casts without gulping blue draughts.

title: Aether Ward
summary: Tier-2 Mage Wardcraft active skill (max rank 4) requiring Chalk Geometry, wrapping the caster in a damage-absorbing ward.

p: Active: Wraps caster in a barrier absorbing 55 damage.

A thin shell of shimmering air that turns aside stray quill-fiend spines and glancing arrows without weighing down the shoulders. It shatters loudly when overloaded, which at least gives the mage fair warning to move.

title: Steady Cadence
summary: Tier-2 Mage Wardcraft passive (max rank 4) requiring Vellum Margin, improving resistance against spell interruption.

p: Reduces spell interruption chance when struck in melee.

Anyone can recite a ward-verse in a quiet library; doing it while a thorn-boar slams into your frontliner takes iron nerves. Steady breathing and a flat tone keep the syllables unbroken even when mud splashes across the page.

title: Unravel Hex
summary: Tier-3 Mage Wardcraft active skill (max rank 3) requiring Aether Ward, dispelling hostile curses and enchantments.

p: Active: Purges curses from allies and strips enemy buffs.

Fen hexers and ash weavers rely on nasty little knots of malice to rot a squad from the inside out. A sharp tug on the loose thread unravels their handiwork in a heartbeat, leaving them with nothing but a crooked stick.

title: Conservation Law
summary: Tier-3 Mage Wardcraft passive (max rank 3) requiring Steady Cadence, granting a chance for spells to cost no mana.

p: Grants a 15% chance for any spell cast to cost zero mana.

Collegium auditors hate waste in any form, whether spilled lamp oil or stray ley-charge. By catching the rebound from a finished cast, a thrifty wardcrafter occasionally fires a follow-up spell completely off the books.

title: Astral Refraction
summary: Tier-4 Mage Wardcraft passive (max rank 3) requiring Unravel Hex, granting broad resistance against all elemental damage.

p: Increases all elemental resistances by +12%.

Rather than blocking fire, frost, or lightning head-on, a refracting ward bends the worst of the impact sideways into the dirt. It scorches the grass around the caster's boots, yet leaves their coat unblemished.

title: Stasis Glyph
summary: Tier-4 Mage Wardcraft capstone (max rank 2) requiring Conservation Law, locking a target in temporary astral stasis.

p: Active: Locks a 3-tile area in frozen time for 3s.

Borrowed from First-Dynasty vault seals designed to keep dangerous relics from decaying. Trapped inside a pale blue glyph, even a charging colossus hangs motionless in mid-stride while the company regroups around it.

title: Reinforced Marrow
summary: Tier-1 Necromancer Bonecraft passive (max rank 5) that increases the maximum health of raised minions.

p: Increases health and armor of raised bone servants.

Freshly raised parish dead are brittle things that snap like dry kindling under a mace. Packing their hollow shins with tallow and lime-dust keeps a skeleton standing through twice as many blows before it needs re-knitting.

title: Sharp Awl
summary: Tier-1 Necromancer Bonecraft passive (max rank 5) that increases damage dealt by bone spells.

p: Increases bone and physical spell damage.

Probate clerks keep a steel awl on their desk for punching vellum tallies; field necromancers file the tip needle-sharp for grim work. Driven by grave-mana, sharpened bone splinters punch cleanly through boiled leather.

title: Marrow Mend
summary: Tier-2 Necromancer Bonecraft active skill (max rank 4) requiring Reinforced Marrow, restoring health to damaged minions.

p: Active: Repairs a bone servant or heals self using a corpse.
Why dig up a fresh corpse in the rain when the one you already bound just needs its ribs wired back together? A quick flick of the wand snaps cracked femurs straight and keeps the frontline marching.

title: Double Entry
summary: Tier-2 Necromancer Bonecraft passive (max rank 2) requiring Sharp Awl, increasing the maximum number of active minions.

p: Allows +1 additional raised servant active at once.

Any lazy clerk can track one debtor; a proper Border bookkeeper runs two columns at once without smudging the ink. Balancing extra bindings strains the temples, yet an extra pair of bony hands always earns its keep.

title: Splintering Rib
summary: Tier-3 Necromancer Bonecraft passive (max rank 4) requiring Marrow Mend, causing bone attacks to inflict bleeding.

p: Bone spells apply 4 bleed damage/s for 4s.
Clean steel cuts neatly and bandages easily; jagged bone fragments break off inside the wound and keep working with every step. Mercenaries on the receiving end rarely complain for long.

title: Bone Spike Eruption
summary: Tier-3 Necromancer Bonecraft active skill (max rank 3) requiring Double Entry, erupting jagged bone spikes beneath foes.

p: Active: Impales foes in a 2.5-tile circle from below.

The northern roads are paved over three centuries of forgotten skirmishes and pauper ditches. Calling up what lies two feet under the mud turns a quiet trail into a forest of pale, razor-sharp stakes.

title: Iron-Shod Femurs
summary: Tier-4 Necromancer Bonecraft passive (max rank 3) requiring Splintering Rib, substantially boosting minion attack damage.

p: Raised servants gain +25% attack damage and armor pen.

Bolting scrap iron bands around skeletal forearms adds weight that living muscles would tire of carrying in ten minutes. Dead servants never complain about sore wrists, and their blows hit like quarry hammers.

title: Golem of Arrears
summary: Tier-4 Necromancer Bonecraft capstone (max rank 2) requiring Bone Spike Eruption, raising a massive high-health bone golem.

p: Active: Assembles a towering bone-bailiff from 3 corpses.

When a whole parish defaults on its tithes, the probate office consolidates the debt into a single hulking frame of wired ribs and ironstone. Slow, silent, and terrifyingly durable, it absorbs punishment meant for an entire squad.

title: Accrued Interest
summary: Tier-1 Necromancer Probate passive (max rank 5) that increases damage-over-time from curses and afflictions.

p: Increases astral and curse damage over time.

On the Border, an unpaid debt never sits still—it compounds quietly while you sleep until it swallows your farm. Probate hexes work the exact same way, gnawing deeper into a foe's vitals with every passing second.

title: Balanced Scales
summary: Tier-1 Necromancer Probate passive (max rank 5) that grants steady regeneration while curses are active.

p: Increases mana regeneration when an enemy is cursed.

Every proper ledger demands that whatever leaves one column must appear in another. As a cursed enemy withers in the mud, a thin trickle of stolen vigor settles neatly onto the necromancer's own side of the page.

title: Writ of Weakness
summary: Tier-2 Necromancer Probate active skill (max rank 4) requiring Accrued Interest, cursing enemies to weaken their attacks.

p: Active: Curses foe, cutting their physical damage by 25%.
Stamped with a phantom wax seal that feels like a millstone hung around the shoulders. Even a charging basalt brute swings sluggishly once a probate clerk reads the terms of his forfeiture aloud.

title: Blood Receipt
summary: Tier-2 Necromancer Probate passive (max rank 4) requiring Balanced Scales, restoring health when cursed enemies die.

p: Restores health whenever a cursed enemy dies.

Closing an account brings a quiet, practical satisfaction to any border bailiff. When a marked foe finally drops, the snapped lien floods back into the caster, knitting scratches and steadying tired legs.

title: Audit the Living
summary: Tier-3 Necromancer Probate passive (max rank 3) requiring Writ of Weakness, lowering resistances on cursed targets.

p: Cursed enemies suffer -15% all resistances.
A thorough auditor finds every hidden crack in a merchant's strongbox and every gap in a knight's plate. Under this scrutiny, elemental wards and thick hides alike peel back like damp paper.

title: Transfer Balance
summary: Tier-3 Necromancer Probate active skill (max rank 3) requiring Blood Receipt, transferring health between units.

p: Active: Shifts health from a bone servant to heal an ally.

Vitality is just another commodity on the frontier, and smart officers move it where the line is thinnest. Siphoning strength across the ledger keeps a failing frontliner upright long enough to seal the breach.

title: Binding Contract
summary: Tier-4 Necromancer Probate passive (max rank 2) requiring Audit the Living, spreading active curses to additional foes.

p: Curses spread to 1 nearby foe when the primary target dies.

Third-Dynasty law held that when a debtor fell, his nearest kin inherited the balance on the spot. In battle, that same cruel clause leaps straight from a dying raider onto the comrade standing beside him.

title: Total Liquidation
summary: Tier-4 Necromancer Probate capstone (max rank 2) requiring Transfer Balance, detonating all active curses for burst damage.

p: Active: Detonates all active curses on target for burst.

No extensions, no grace periods, and no appeals—just every outstanding hex called in simultaneously with a deafening crack. Whole packs of weakened foes fold at once when the clerk slams the book shut.

title: Salt Preservative
summary: Tier-1 Necromancer Abbey passive (max rank 5) that grants cold and poison resistance.

p: Grants cold and poison resistance.

Coastal abbey sextons pack their shrouds in coarse sea-salt and dried rue to keep crypt-damp and marsh-fever out of their lungs. It stings the eyes at first, yet it lets a watcher work through winter fog unharmed.

title: Witness's Calm
summary: Tier-1 Necromancer Abbey passive (max rank 5) that increases mind resistance against mental and astral effects.

p: Increases Mind and silence resistance.

Sitting vigil beside drowned sailors teaches a monk to ignore whispers in the dark. After a few years of listening to tide-bells and restless spirits, ordinary battlefield terror barely raises the pulse.

title: Censer Fumes
summary: Tier-2 Necromancer Abbey active skill (max rank 4) requiring Salt Preservative, releasing censer fumes that slow enemies.

p: Active: Emits incense smoke that slows foes in 3 tiles.
Swinging a heavy bronze pot packed with damp peat-resin and bitter herbs rolls a thick gray fog across the flagstones. Charging raiders cough, stumble, and lose their momentum inside the acrid cloud.

title: Last Rites
summary: Tier-2 Necromancer Abbey passive (max rank 1) requiring Witness's Calm, sealing corpses to prevent enemy revivals.

p: Prevents slain enemies from being revived by enemy shamans.
A quiet word, a pinch of quicklime, and a thumb pressed to the brow—simple parish work that ruins an ash-tongue shaman's whole afternoon. Once sealed by an abbey arbiter, the dead stay decently dead.

title: Vow of Quiet
summary: Tier-3 Necromancer Abbey passive (max rank 3) requiring Censer Fumes, projecting an aura that reduces shadow damage.

p: Nearby allies take 12% reduced astral and shadow damage.
Where an oath-keeper stands, the chill of the ossuary loses its teeth. Allies fighting within earshot of his quiet liturgy find dark curses sliding off their armor like rain off greased canvas.

title: Dismiss the Watch
summary: Tier-3 Necromancer Abbey active skill (max rank 3) requiring Last Rites, dealing heavy banishing damage to enemies.

p: Active: Banishes summoned foes and deals heavy astral dmg.
Delivered with the flat finality of a bell tolling the end of a watch. Undead husks and summoned horrors shudder and break apart under the formal command to vacate the premises.

title: Keeper of Oaths
summary: Tier-4 Necromancer Abbey passive (max rank 3) requiring Vow of Quiet, amplifying the caster's healing power.

p: Increases healing and shield effectiveness by +20%.
Not all abbey clerks deal only in coffins; many spent years tending frostbitten fishermen and bruised levy-men. Their steady, unhurried mendings stretch meager bandages and scarce mana twice as far.

title: Final Reckoning
summary: Tier-4 Necromancer Abbey capstone (max rank 2) requiring Dismiss the Watch, forging a lasting spiritual link on the field.

p: Active: Links allies for 6s, splitting damage and healing all.

The oldest liturgy of the coastal abbeys, spoken only when the seawall is cracking and retreat is off the table. Bound together in solemn witness, the company endures blows that would scatter lesser troops.
